learningObjectives.title: Beliefs about God and the articles of faith

questions.q: What does the Islamic term 'Tawhid' mean?
questions.explain: Tawhid is the belief in the absolute oneness and unity of Allah, the most important belief in Islam.

questions.q: How many articles of faith are traditionally accepted in Sunni Islam?
questions.explain: The six articles are belief in Allah, angels, holy books, prophets, the Day of Judgement and predestination.

questions.q: According to Muslim belief, which angel revealed the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad?
questions.explain: The angel Jibril (Gabriel) delivered the revelation of the Qur'an to Muhammad.

questions.q: How many Pillars of Islam are there?
questions.explain: The Five Pillars are Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm and Hajj.

questions.q: What proportion of a Muslim's qualifying wealth is normally given as Zakah?
questions.explain: Zakah is the giving of 2.5% of a Muslim's surplus wealth and savings each year.

questions.q: During which month of the Islamic calendar do Muslims perform the fast of Sawm?
questions.explain: Sawm is the obligatory fasting undertaken from dawn to sunset throughout the month of Ramadan.

questions.q: What is the name for the direction Muslims face when they pray?
questions.explain: The Qiblah is the direction of the Ka'bah in Makkah, which Muslims face during salah.

questions.q: What is the name of the special congregational prayer held at the mosque on Fridays?
questions.explain: Jummah is the Friday midday congregational prayer that Muslim men are expected to attend at the mosque.

questions.q: In Islam, what is meant by the sin of 'shirk'?
questions.explain: Shirk is regarded as the gravest sin because it denies the oneness of Allah by treating something else as equal to God.

questions.q: Muhammad is described as the 'Seal of the Prophets'. What does this mean?
questions.explain: Muslims believe Muhammad is the last of the prophets, completing the messages given to earlier prophets.

questions.q: What do Muslims believe about Akhirah (the Day of Judgement)?
options: All people will be judged by Allah after death
The world will never come to an end
questions.explain: Muslims believe that after death everyone will be resurrected and judged by Allah, leading to Paradise or Hell.

questions.q: Which statement best expresses the meaning of the Shahadah?
options: There is no god but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah
Muslims should give 2.5% of their wealth
Every Muslim must travel to Makkah
questions.explain: The Shahadah is the declaration of faith affirming belief in one God and the prophethood of Muhammad.

questions.q: For which Muslims is Hajj an obligation?
options: Those who are physically and financially able, at least once in a lifetime
Only those who can recite the whole Qur'an
Only those who already live in Makkah
questions.explain: Hajj is compulsory once in a lifetime for every Muslim who is healthy enough and can afford to go.

questions.q: Why do Muslims perform wudu before salah?
options: To achieve ritual purity before prayer
To announce the start of prayer
questions.explain: Wudu is the ritual washing that prepares a Muslim to stand in a state of cleanliness before Allah in prayer.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the mihrab in a mosque?
options: A niche showing the direction of Makkah
A tower used for the call to prayer
An area for washing before prayer
A platform for delivering the sermon
questions.explain: The mihrab is an alcove in the qiblah wall that indicates the direction of Makkah for worshippers.

questions.q: What does the festival of Eid ul-Fitr celebrate?
options: The end of the fast of Ramadan
The completion of the Hajj pilgrimage
The willingness of Ibrahim to sacrifice his son
The first revelation of the Qur'an
questions.explain: Eid ul-Fitr, the 'festival of breaking the fast', joyfully marks the completion of the month of Ramadan.

questions.q: Aisha is pregnant and is worried about fasting during Ramadan. According to Islamic teaching, what is her position?
options: She must fast as normal with no exception
She is permitted not to fast and may make up the days later
She can never make up the missed fast
Fasting is forbidden for all women
questions.explain: Pregnant women are exempt from fasting if it may harm them, and can make up the missed days at a later time.

questions.q: A festival involves the sacrifice of an animal (qurbani) and recalls Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son. Which festival is this?
questions.explain: Eid ul-Adha, the 'festival of sacrifice', occurs during Hajj and commemorates Ibrahim's obedience to Allah.

questions.q: A Muslim has £2,000 in qualifying savings that has been held for a year. How much should be given as Zakah?
questions.explain: Zakah is 2.5% of qualifying wealth, and 2.5% of £2,000 is £50.

questions.q: Yusuf sincerely declares 'There is no god but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah' in order to become a Muslim. Which pillar is he performing?
questions.explain: Reciting and believing the declaration of faith is the Shahadah, the first Pillar of Islam.
